Compare the columns of two tables

Source: R/columns.R
compare_columns.Rd

The schema view of a comparison: which columns each table has, their types, and how much their values overlap. It reads every column of both tables, including the ones diff_table() would drop, so it is the place to look when a comparison refuses to run.

compare_columns(x, y)

Arguments

x, y

Tables to compare: data.frames or data.tables.

Value

A data.table with one row per column of either side: the normalized name colname, the names as written in each table (name_x, name_y), the two types and whether they match, the two unique counts, and the value overlap (n_common, n_union, over_pct). Rows follow x's column order, then whatever is only in y. A column missing from one side has NA for that side.

Details

Column names are normalized first, as diff_table() does: upper case, with every run of other characters replaced by _. So amount in x and Amount in y are one column. Two names in one table that normalize to the same thing are an error.

over_pct is the distinct values shared by both sides over the distinct values seen in either, n_common / n_union. 100 means the two columns draw on exactly the same set of values; a value y invents or one it never uses both pull it down.

The overlap is measured only where the two types agree. %in% coerces before matching, so a numeric 1 would count as a match for the string "1" and two columns that are not the same thing would report a full overlap. A column whose type differs gets NA for n_common, n_union and over_pct.

Examples

x <- data.frame(id = 1:3, amount = c(1, 2, 3))
y <- data.frame(ID = c(1L, 2L, 4L), Amount = c("1", "2", "3"), note = "a")
compare_columns(x, y)
#>    colname name_x name_y  type_x    type_y type_match n_unique_x n_unique_y
#>     <char> <char> <char>  <char>    <char>     <lgcl>      <int>      <int>
#> 1:      ID     id     ID integer   integer       TRUE          3          3
#> 2:  AMOUNT amount Amount numeric character      FALSE          3          3
#> 3:    NOTE   <NA>   note    <NA> character         NA         NA          1
#>    n_common n_union over_pct
#>       <int>   <int>    <num>
#> 1:        2       4       50
#> 2:       NA      NA       NA
#> 3:       NA      NA       NA
